title: Region Affinity Governor and Retention Proof Export for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers operating under data residency commitments need deterministic controls that ensure requests are served from allowed regions, tenant-level retention guarantees, and a machine-readable proof bundle for audits. Current hosted endpoints offer informal region hints and a per-tenant retention flag but lack deterministic routing guarantees, configurable soft-fail behavior, and an automated evidence export that packages placement + retention proofs for auditors.

Goal: Deliver a combined feature set we are calling the Region Affinity Governor: an API + Console surface that lets operators declare per-tenant locality constraints (allowed regions, preferred regions, fallback policy), retention profiles per route (TTL, token-level retention exemptions), and an automated Proof Export pipeline that produces tamper-evident evidence bundles (manifest, signed hashes, serving logs snapshot, retention decisions) for a requested time window. The feature must integrate with the existing routing layer, the Console rollout controls, and the compliance export pipeline so customers can schedule or on-demand export a compliance package for a tenant or route.
acceptance_criteria: API: New endpoints to set tenant locality policy with parameters: allowed_regions, affinity_score, fallback_policy (soft-fail|strict|convert-to-dedicated)
Console: UI to view and edit locality policies with validation and an impact preview overlay showing % of recent requests that would be affected
Serving: Requests evaluated against locality policy before routing; when strict and no capacity in allowed regions, request is rejected with structured error code RESIDENCY_VIOLATION
Retention: Per-route retention profiles applied at ingress; retention metadata persisted and surfaced in token-level billing & logs

Proof Export: Exported bundle includes manifest.json, signed index of objects, route-level retention decisions, per-request routing trace (redacted with PII rules), and SHA256 manifests; export stored to a tenant S3 bucket or provided as downloadable signed bundle
Docs & SDK: SDK methods and Console help pages published; sample compliance bundle unpacker script in repo
implementation_notes: Add new database table tenant_locality_policies (tenant_id, allowed_regions, preferred_regions, affinity_score, fallback_policy, created_by, created_at)
Routing change: early-policy-evaluator middleware that reads policy and marks request.preference_region and request.enforcement_mode before kernel selection
Soft-fail behaviour: when fallback_policy=soft-fail, prefer allowed regions but allow routing to nearest compatible region with annotated reason and add to proof bundle
Retention metadata will be recorded as a lightweight header on the request and persisted to the request events stream (kafka) for later inclusion in compliance bundles

Proof Export pipeline: lambda/worker that pulls request traces + retention decisions for time window, creates a manifest, computes SHA256 of each artifact, stores artifacts to export bucket, and records signed manifest via KMS RSA signing key
Console: affinity preview uses sampled logs (30d window, sample rate 1%) to estimate impact and cost delta; preview must not expose raw PII and runs in a readonly analytics datastore
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): API + Console edit, proof export MVP, restricted to a small set of compliance customers
Phase 2 (customer opt-in): expose UI self-serve, add SDK helpers and example unpacker, collect feedback on soft-fail UX
Phase 3 (GA): enable default retention profiles, enable scheduled exports, add SLA language to Dedicated conversion flow
Backout plan: admins can disable enforcement per-tenant to revert to previous best-effort routing

qa_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation with 3 region scenarios and both soft-fail and strict modes
Integration test: end-to-end export for a 24h window with injected traces and validation of signed manifest
E2E: Console edit -> simulate preview -> apply -> verify routing decisions in staging cluster using canary traffic
Security: verify proof bundle signing, expiry, and read-access controls for tenant S3 buckets
risks: Risk: Soft-fail might cause customers to unintentionally violate residency contracts if they misunderstand preview; mitigation: explicit modal warning and require explicit opt-in
Risk: Proof bundles may contain PII if redaction rules are incomplete; mitigation: reuse existing PII redactors and add explicit QA step
Risk: KMS signing key availability becomes single point of failure for export; mitigation: rotate to multi-region KMS and add retry/backoff logic
metrics: Percentage of requests served outside allowed regions (target 0% for strict mode)
Number of exported proof bundles per week
Time to generate a proof bundle for 30d window (target < 10 minutes)
Customer-reported compliance incidents related to residency (target 0 after GA)
